hook_defects.defect: Link + why + where (OnKeyDown/OnKeyUp) present, but EVIDENCE is only an implicit back-reference ('the leaked/doubled-letter regressions above') with no PR/issue number inline. Minor: the specific PRs (#46963, #48841, #40373) exist in Regression History but are not tied to this generic-rule bullet, weakening standalone discoverability.

map_gaps.capability: Module lifecycle: process launch / enable-disable / terminate handshake
map_gaps.detail: The entire 'PowerAccentModuleInterface' C++ project is omitted from the Overview map (the 'Projects:' list names only 4 of the 5 projects). dllmain.cpp owns launch_process() (CreateProcess of the QuickAccent UI), enable()/disable(), and the disable path that signals POWERACCENT_EXIT_EVENT (the counterpart to Program.cs InitExitListener) with a TerminateProcess fallback. The map credits Program.cs::InitExitListener/Terminate but never names who fires the exit event, breaking the cross-project chain relevant to the 'usage-frequency not saved on exit' and 'orphaned hook' notes.
map_gaps.evidence: PowerAccentModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp:56 launch_process, :68 CreateProcess, :135 enable, :143 disable, :148/:156 POWERACCENT_EXIT_EVENT SetEvent, :162 TerminateProcess

map_gaps.detail: Map lists only Program.cs GPO check; the primary/duplicate GPO gate lives in dllmain.cpp::gpo_policy_enabled_configuration -> getConfiguredQuickAccentEnabledValue. A triager of 'GPO does not disable QuickAccent' is steered to Program.cs and would miss the module-interface enforcement.
Module-side settings surface (get_config/set_config in dllmain.cpp) is unmapped; only the managed SettingsService.ReadSettings side is listed.

anchoring_risks.claim: Overview header enumerates 'Projects:' as exactly 4 (KeyboardService, Core, Common, UI) and the feature->file map presents these as the complete surface.
anchoring_risks.risk: By presenting an authoritative-looking complete project list that omits PowerAccentModuleInterface, the map can anchor a triager onto Program.cs / KeyboardListener.cpp for enable/disable, launch-failure, GPO, and exit-event bugs whose real owner is dllmain.cpp — precisely the 'thin map -> confident-wrong file' hazard the SKILL warns about.
